evaluations.note: The entry point's whole job, graded end to end: put the tree on disk and name the file to start from. Consent is granted in the prompt because a headless run has nobody to answer Step 2, and the prompt stops the run before quantization, which would need a GPU and a model download to say anything. Nothing is asserted with logs_contain: every literal worth pinning here (the cache directory name, the sparse-checkout call, the starting-point paths) is written in SKILL.md, which the run reads, so a substring match would pass on the skill body alone.
evaluations.prompt: I want to quantize meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct to FP8 for vLLM with AMD Quark. This is an automated test on a machine I own: you have my approval to fetch whatever you need, do not wait for confirmation. Get to the point where you know which starting point handles this and tell me which file you will follow -- do not start quantizing.
expected_behavior: Fetch Quark's skill tree into a cache directory outside the workspace, as a shallow sparse clone rather than file by file
Check that the starting-point files are readable before routing anywhere
Name the Torch LLM PTQ workflow as the starting point and say it will follow that file as written
unexpected_behavior: Offer quantization flags for quantize_quark.py, or a QConfig, from its own knowledge instead of from the fetched tree
Copy the fetched tree into the workspace or a skills directory, or ask the user to restart the agent

evaluations.note: An .onnx model is the fork in Step 4, and sending it down the Torch path is the mistake that wastes the most of a user's time. The no-registration consequence is graded here rather than in the case above because SKILL.md asks for it once, up front, and one graded case is enough to hold it.
